extracted.intended_audience: architects, art historians, critics, and educated readers evaluating Byzantine/Venetian incrusted architecture (e.g., St. Mark's)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for judging St. Mark's and similar incrusted (brick-faced-with-precious-stone) buildings: first assess construction and decorative/artistic merit, then evaluate fitness for religious use and effect on worshippers. Emphasizes material causes, chromatic perception, honesty of facing, and detailing rules for incrusted work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twofold inquiry: art first, then worship
rubrics_metrics.description: We have first to judge of St. Mark's merely as a piece of architecture, not as a church; secondly, to estimate its fitness for its special duty as a place of worship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the study of expression distinct from abstract architectural perfection: form/construction/decorative merit should be assessed on purely artistic grounds before considering expressional/ritual fitness or influence on devotional feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incrustation as the dominant characteristic
rubrics_metrics.description: The first broad characteristic of the building, and the root nearly of every other important peculiarity in it, is its confessed 'incrustation' — the ruling principle is the incrustation of brick with more precious materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand that the system of decoration and the arrangement of parts are founded upon this duplicity of substance (inner brick vs outer facing); criticisms should be framed by this fundamental fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between incrusted and massive styles
rubrics_metrics.description: Two generally distinct families of buildings: (1) substance alike throughout (massive) and (2) substance of two kinds, internal and external (incrusted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize legitimate characteristics of each style (e.g., Greek/early Norman/Gothic as solid; St. Mark's as incrusted). Intermediate examples exist but should not confuse the basic typological differences when judging design choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty of incrustation (duplicity is not insincerity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Southern builders fastened every slab of facial marble by a confessed 'rivet', and the joints of the armor are visibly accommodated to the contours of the substance within.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not condemn incrustation as dishonest; evaluate its openness and craft (visible attachment, rivets, binding courses) — the external facing should show how it is attached and not pretend to be the whole thickness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material and practical causes must inform stylistic judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural circumstances (distance from quarries, precarious access to stone, small ship tonnage, cost and labor of carriage) give rise to the incrusted method — making each shipload as valuable as possible and encouraging import of sculptured fragments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism should account for economic/physical constraints of builders (transport, scarcity, reuse of ancient fragments) as legitimate determinants of form and method, rather than judge by northern solid-building norms alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for preserving and displaying ancient fragments
rubrics_metrics.description: An architect who cared for the preservation of noble work would have saved every relic with which he was entrusted, rather than sawing old marbles into fragments to avoid interference with his own designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value the architect's choice to incorporate and display reused sculpture and fragments as an ethical and aesthetic decision that can enhance splendor and historical association; preservation is a positive criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colour-perception is prerequisite for true judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The very first requisite for true judgment of St. Mark's is the perfection of that color-faculty which few people ever set themselves seriously to find out whether they possess or not; a deaf man might as well pretend to pronounce judgment on the merits of a full orchestra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors must be able to perceive and appreciate color; architects or critics trained only in form will fail to discern the chief claims of incrusted/colorful buildings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incrusted school as the only one enabling permanent chromatic decoration
rubrics_metrics.description: The school of incrusted architecture is the only one in which perfect and permanent chromatic decoration is possible; regard each piece of jasper and alabaster as a 'cake of very hard color'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat facing marbles and porphyries as enduring color material to be 'ground down' or cut to paint walls with; evaluate composition and color-relationships as central design criteria, with brick as the muscular support clothed by marble.

rubrics_metrics.name: LAW I: Plinths and binding cornices must be light and delicate
rubrics_metrics.description: That the plinths and cornices used for binding the armor are to be light and delicate. A certain thickness (at least two or three inches) is required to prevent fracture, and the pieces must not be merely glued to the rough brick surface but connected with the mass by binding cornices and string courses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design rules: (a) facing pieces need minimal thickness for durability; (b) do not trust cement alone — use mechanical connection (binding courses, rivets) and mutual support; (c) binding plinths/string courses must be visibly incapable of bearing heavy structural work and should be slight so as not to be mistaken for principal cornices of solid construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware architectural 'stage properties' that create false awe
rubrics_metrics.description: Darkness and mystery; confused recesses of building; artificial light employed in small quantity but maintained with constancy; preciousness of material easily comprehended by the vulgar eye; close air loaded with a sweet and peculiar odor; solemn music; and tangible idols — these are the stage properties of superstition assembled in St. Mark's.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a church's religious effect, distinguish between attributes that genuinely convey scriptural/architectural meaning and those that merely produce popular 'false awe'. A successful sacred building should promote comprehension of its histories and doctrines, not rely solely on sensory spectacle.
